meta.title: Catch'em Pokemon TCG English Sets Database
meta.scope: English-language main expansions and notable special sets only. Japanese-exclusive sets, McDonald's promos, and POP series promo sets excluded.
meta.session_1_coverage: Original Series through Black & White Series (1999-2013)
meta.session_2_coverage: XY Series through Mega Evolution Series (2014-2026) — COMPLETE
sources: Wikipedia (List of Pokémon Trading Card Game sets)

schema_notes.card_count: main set count; secret rares and special rarities flagged in notes when relevant
schema_notes.archetype_tags: Catch'em internal classification for app filtering
schema_notes.flag_review: true = data partially uncertain, verify before public use
schema_notes.market_notes: Optional field: contextual observations about the set's market behavior. Should be dated and sourced. Used for editorial/newsletter context, not displayed in app UI by default. May be added to any set as relevant data emerges.

schema_enhancements_apr21_audit.purpose: Prevents citing SKUs that don't exist. Critical for app filtering and newsletter accuracy. Rule: special/mini-set expansions (Hidden Fates, Shining Fates, Champion's Path, Celebrations, Crown Zenith, Paldean Fates, Shrouded Fable, Prismatic Evolutions, Dragon Majesty, Shining Legends, Detective Pikachu, and ALL Mega Evolution special expansions) do NOT have standalone Booster Boxes. Sold only via ETBs, Bundles, Collections, Tins.

eras.character: Foundation era. Short print runs, iconic art, vintage-grade scarcity. Final sets (Skyridge especially) are among the rarest in the hobby.

sets.name: Base Set
sets.notes: The first set. 1st Edition and Shadowless prints carry massive premiums. Charizard is the defining vintage grail.

sets.name: Jungle
sets.notes: Second English set. Introduced the original Eeveelutions as holos. 1st Edition prints premium.

sets.name: Fossil
sets.notes: Third English set. First appearance of Gen 1 fossils in TCG. 1st Edition prints premium.

sets.name: Base Set 2
sets.notes: Reprint set combining highlights from Base Set and Jungle. Generally less desirable than originals, but clean holos still command value.

sets.name: Team Rocket
sets.notes: Introduced 'Dark' Pokemon type. First secret rare in English TCG (Dark Raichu, 83/82). Strong collector base.

sets.name: Gym Heroes
sets.notes: First of the two-set Gym block. Themed around Kanto Gym Leaders. Holos widely available but specific cards (Misty's Tentacruel) valuable.

sets.name: Gym Challenge
sets.notes: Second Gym set. Contains Blaine's Charizard — one of the strongest vintage chase cards outside Base Set.

sets.name: Neo Genesis
sets.notes: First Gen 2 / Johto set. Neo Genesis Lugia is one of the most sought-after modern vintage chases. 1st Edition prints premium.

sets.name: Neo Discovery
sets.notes: First English TCG appearance of Espeon and Umbreon. Historical significance for Eeveelution collectors.

sets.name: Neo Revelation
sets.notes: First Shining Pokemon cards in English TCG. Shining Gyarados and Shining Magikarp are defining chase cards. Low print run.

sets.name: Neo Destiny
sets.notes: Contains Shining Charizard — one of the most iconic and valuable vintage chase cards. Extremely scarce in gem mint condition.

sets.name: Legendary Collection
sets.notes: Reprint compilation of Base/Jungle/Fossil/Team Rocket highlights. Introduced reverse holo. Reverse holo Charizard is a hidden grail.

sets.name: Expedition Base Set
sets.notes: First e-Card set. Introduced Supporters and Stadiums as card types. New layout, slimmer borders. e-Reader compatibility required Japanese hardware in US.

sets.name: Aquapolis
sets.notes: Introduced Crystal Type Pokemon — a collector-favorite rarity. Crystal Charizard from Aquapolis is a high-grade vintage chase. Scarce print.

sets.name: Skyridge
sets.notes: Last WOTC-published set. Extraordinarily low print run made Skyridge one of the rarest and most valuable modern vintage sets. Crystal Charizard is the grail. Sealed boxes sell for high 5 figures.

eras.character: TPCi takes over from WOTC. Powerful Pokemon-ex mechanic introduces prize-card risk/reward. Delta Species and Gold Star chase cards are defining rarities of the era. Gen 3 (Hoenn) Pokemon central, with Gen 1-2 reprints through Delta Species treatment.

sets.name: EX Ruby & Sapphire
sets.notes: First set by TPCi (Pokemon USA). Introduced the Pokemon-ex mechanic. Defines the era's start.

sets.name: EX Sandstorm
sets.notes: Second EX set. Themed around desert Pokemon.

sets.name: EX Dragon
sets.notes: Dragon-themed EX set. First appearance of Rayquaza ex, a definitive chase card.

sets.name: EX Team Magma vs Team Aqua
sets.notes: Themed around the rival teams from Ruby/Sapphire games. Cards explicitly belong to one faction or the other.

sets.name: EX Hidden Legends
sets.notes: Features the Hoenn legendaries. Regi trio first TCG appearance.

sets.name: EX FireRed & LeafGreen
sets.notes: First major Gen 1 callback set under TPCi. Kanto starters as ex. Strong collector nostalgia value.

sets.name: EX Team Rocket Returns
sets.notes: Introduced the Gold Star rarity — shiny-variant Pokemon with starred rarity symbol. Gold Stars are among the most valuable EX-era chase cards. Legendary beasts trio as Gold Stars.

sets.name: EX Deoxys
sets.notes: Rayquaza Gold Star from this set is a defining EX-era grail. Deoxys featured in all four forms.

sets.name: EX Emerald
sets.notes: Features Gold Star Magikarp and Gyarados — a paired collector's duo prized together.

sets.name: EX Unseen Forces
sets.notes: Contains Espeon and Umbreon Gold Stars — among the most valuable and coveted cards of the EX era. Full Unown alphabet + punctuation. Large set.

sets.name: EX Delta Species
sets.notes: Introduced Delta Species mechanic — Pokemon with alternate typings (e.g., Fire-type Pikachu). Delta Species defines the next four EX sets.

sets.name: EX Legend Maker
sets.notes: Smaller set. Continues Delta Species line. Mew ex is the notable chase.

sets.name: EX Holon Phantoms
sets.notes: Contains three Gold Stars including Pikachu Gold Star — one of the most sought-after Pikachu cards in the TCG.

sets.name: EX Crystal Guardians
sets.notes: Second Kanto starter homage through Delta Species variants. Collector-favorite Delta cards.

sets.name: EX Dragon Frontiers
sets.notes: Contains Rayquaza Gold Star (Delta Species variant) — a distinct and valuable chase separate from EX Deoxys Rayquaza Gold Star.

sets.name: EX Power Keepers
sets.notes: Final EX Series set and final Gen 3 set. Reprint-heavy. Loosely themed around Hoenn Elite Four.

eras.character: Gen 4 / Sinnoh era. Pokemon LV.X mechanic replaces ex. Lost Zone introduced in Platinum. Established the 4-sets-per-year quarterly cadence that still defines the modern schedule. Pokemon-SP subtype is the era's competitive hallmark.

sets.name: Diamond & Pearl
sets.notes: First Gen 4 / Sinnoh set. Introduced Pokemon LV.X mechanic. Release date varies by source (May 3 or May 23, 2007).

sets.name: Mysterious Treasures
sets.notes: Second D&P set. Introduces 'Pokemon with Item' mechanic — Pokemon with held items integrated.

sets.name: Secret Wonders
sets.notes: Third D&P set. Mewtwo LV.X is the featured chase. Strong competitive cards.

sets.name: Great Encounters
sets.notes: Introduces Leafeon and Glaceon — the two newest Eeveelutions — to the TCG as LV.X chases.

sets.name: Majestic Dawn
sets.notes: Introduces Pokemon G subtype. Smaller set.

sets.name: Legends Awakened
sets.notes: Fourth-largest set in TCG history at the time. Seven Pokemon LV.X cards — more than any prior set.

sets.name: Stormfront
sets.notes: Final D&P-branded set. Stormfront Charizard is a fan-favorite chase. Sableye SF became a competitive staple (Turn 1 'Trick or Trap').

sets.name: Platinum
sets.notes: Introduced Lost Zone (cards removed from play permanently) and Pokemon-SP mechanic. Major competitive shift.

sets.name: Rising Rivals
sets.notes: Expands Pokemon-SP subtypes. Luxray GL LV.X is competitive hallmark of the era.

sets.name: Supreme Victors
sets.notes: Garchomp C LV.X defines the late-SP meta. Largest D&P/Platinum set.

sets.name: Arceus
sets.notes: Final Platinum set. Three Arceus LV.X variants (Fighting, Grass, Lightning). Spiritomb was the SP-killer of the meta.

eras.character: Short era (5 sets). Returns to Johto / Gen 2 roots with remakes as the theme. Pokemon Prime and LEGEND cards are the defining rarities — Prime has holo backgrounds, LEGEND cards are two-card sets that form one full artwork. Call of Legends closes the era with Shiny Pokemon reprints.

sets.name: HeartGold & SoulSilver
sets.notes: Introduced Pokemon Prime and Pokemon LEGEND mechanics. LEGEND cards are split across two cards that form one artwork. Highly collectible era.

sets.name: HS Unleashed
sets.notes: Tyranitar Prime is the defining chase of this set. Beloved by Johto collectors.

sets.name: HS Undaunted
sets.notes: Contains Espeon Prime and Umbreon Prime — two of the most valuable and sought-after modern-vintage cards. Tyrogue also an iconic chase.

sets.name: HS Triumphant
sets.notes: Mew Prime and Gengar Prime are the headliners. Final HGSS-branded main set.

sets.name: Call of Legends
sets.notes: Transition set bridging HGSS and Black & White eras. Features reprint Shiny Legendary Pokemon as secret rares. Treated as its own mini-series.

eras.character: Gen 5 / Unova era. Introduced full-art Pokemon and Supporters — the first era where full arts became standard chase targets. Pokemon-EX mechanic reintroduced (replacing LV.X) as the competitive and collector centerpiece. Team Plasma storyline carried through multiple sets. Pokemon TCG Online launched during this era.

sets.name: Black & White
sets.notes: First Gen 5 set. Introduced full-art cards — a visual hallmark still used today. Reshiram and Zekrom debut.

sets.name: Emerging Powers
sets.notes: Second B&W set. No Pokemon-EX or special rarities yet. Competitive-focused.

sets.name: Noble Victories
sets.notes: N Supporter card from this set became the most iconic Trainer card of the era. Swords of Justice trio featured.

sets.name: Next Destinies
sets.notes: Reintroduced Pokemon-EX mechanic in the modern format. Mewtwo EX was the defining chase and competitive staple of the era.

sets.name: Dark Explorers
sets.notes: Darkrai EX defined the post-2012 meta. Strong competitive set. Landorus EX equally impactful.

sets.name: Dragons Exalted
sets.notes: Introduced the Dragon type to the TCG. Rayquaza EX defined a major competitive archetype.

sets.name: Dragon Vault
sets.notes: Mini-set with 20 Dragon-type reprints. Sold in small promotional packs, not as a standalone main release.

sets.name: Boundaries Crossed
sets.notes: Introduced ACE SPEC — powerful Trainer cards limited to one per deck. Keldeo EX was a competitive keystone paired with Black Kyurem.

sets.name: Plasma Storm
sets.notes: Start of Team Plasma three-set arc. Team Plasma Pokemon have unique interactions with themed Trainers.

sets.name: Plasma Freeze
sets.notes: Second Team Plasma set. Deoxys EX + Kyurem EX formed competitive archetype.

sets.name: Plasma Blast
sets.notes: Final Team Plasma set. Ho-Oh EX and Lugia EX closed the era with a Johto legendary callback.

sets.name: Legendary Treasures
sets.notes: Compilation set closing the B&W era. Contains the Radiant Collection — 25 bonus cards with shiny/alternate treatments. Precursor concept to later 'trainer gallery' sub-sets.

eras.character: Gen VI. Introduced Pokémon-EX with Mega Evolution mechanic (M-EX) and the Fairy type to TCG. 20th anniversary celebrated mid-era with Generations and Evolutions sets. Strong Charizard-chase era (Flashfire, Evolutions). BREAK cards introduced late-era.

sets.name: Kalos Starter Set
sets.notes: Small preview set released ahead of XY base set. Contained 3 fixed starter decks. Not a standard expansion — primarily teaching/onboarding product.

sets.name: XY
sets.notes: Base set of the XY era. Introduced Fairy type, Mega Evolution cards, and Gen VI Pokémon to TCG. 146 cards in English release (larger than Japanese 126).

sets.name: Flashfire
sets.notes: The Charizard set of the XY era. Features two Mega Charizard-EX cards (one Fire-type M-EX, one Dragon-type M-EX). Major chase set for Charizard collectors.

sets.name: Furious Fists
sets.notes: Fighting-type themed set. Seismitoad-EX became a defining competitive card in standard format. Lucario holds strong nostalgia value.

sets.name: Phantom Forces
sets.notes: Introduced VS Seeker, one of the most impactful Trainer cards in TCG history. Team Flare sub-theme reflected Gen VI villain faction.

sets.name: Primal Clash
sets.notes: Massive 160-card set. Introduced Primal Reversion mechanic (distinct from Mega Evolution). Hoenn remake tie-in. Ancient Trait abilities debuted.

sets.name: Double Crisis
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. Small 34-card themed mini-set. Team Magma vs Team Aqua. Sold only in themed special blisters and collections, never standalone booster boxes.

sets.name: Roaring Skies
sets.notes: Shaymin-EX 'Set Up' became a defining engine card for years of competitive play. M Rayquaza-EX also saw heavy competitive use. Strong chase set.

sets.name: Ancient Origins
sets.notes: Notable for reviving Giratina-EX and featuring ancient Pokémon. Smaller set size (98 cards).

sets.name: BREAKthrough
sets.notes: Introduced Pokémon BREAK mechanic — golden landscape-oriented evolution cards. Two Mega Mewtwo-EX cards headlined the set. Large 164-card count.

sets.name: BREAKpoint
sets.notes: Greninja BREAK became one of the defining competitive archetypes ('Greninja BREAK deck') in late XY format.

sets.name: Generations
key_mechanics: Radiant Collection sub-set with full-art variants
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. 20th Anniversary special set. 83 main cards + 32-card Radiant Collection sub-set. Only available through 20th Anniversary promo collections initially. Not sold as standalone booster boxes.

sets.name: Fates Collide
sets.notes: Penultimate-year XY set. Alakazam and Zygarde themed. Moderate competitive impact.

sets.name: Steam Siege
sets.notes: Introduced Volcanion-EX (tied to Volcanion movie promotion). Magearna-EX also featured as Mythical Pokémon debut.

sets.name: Evolutions
sets.notes: 20th anniversary capstone set. Reimagines the original 1999 Base Set with modern card stock, yellow borders, hand-drawn energy symbols. The M Charizard-EX Full Art is the defining chase. Three ETB variants (Charizard/Blastoise/Venusaur) now collectible sealed. Modern set with vintage aesthetic.

eras.character: Gen VII. Introduced Pokémon-GX (similar to EX but with GX Attacks — once per game high-impact moves). Special 'Fates' sets revived Shiny Pokémon collecting. Cosmic Eclipse closed the era with TAG TEAM mechanic and largest set of the era.

sets.name: Sun & Moon
sets.notes: Base set introducing the GX mechanic. Alolan starter trio as GX cards. Marked a shift in card design and art direction.

sets.name: Guardians Rising
sets.notes: Tapu Lele-GX became one of the most-played competitive cards of the GX era (its ability to grab Supporter cards). Tapus themed set tied to Alola region.

sets.name: Burning Shadows
sets.notes: Rainbow Rare Charizard-GX is one of the signature cards of the Sun & Moon era. Heavy chase value. Gardevoir-GX spawned a defining competitive archetype.

sets.name: Shining Legends
sets.notes: Small special set focusing on Shining variants of Legendary and Mythical Pokémon. Not sold in standard booster boxes — available through special collections and 3-pack blisters.

sets.name: Crimson Invasion
sets.notes: Ultra Beast themed set from the Ultra Sun/Ultra Moon games. Silvally-GX as legendary ally. Smaller set size than surrounding releases.

sets.name: Ultra Prism
sets.notes: Introduced Prism Star ♦ cards — unique powerful cards limited to one copy per deck. Full-art Gen IV Trainers (Cynthia, Cyrus) became staples.

sets.name: Forbidden Light
sets.notes: Malamar + Ultra Necrozma-GX combo became a dominant Psychic-type archetype. Zygarde-GX also featured.

sets.name: Celestial Storm
sets.notes: Rayquaza-GX became a top-tier competitive deck. Stunning full-art Trainers (Lana, Mallow, Steven) were major collector targets.

sets.name: Dragon Majesty
sets.notes: Dragon-type themed special set. Every card in the set has a foil treatment. Only sold through special collections and pin blisters — no booster boxes. 70 main cards + 8 secret rares.

sets.name: Lost Thunder
sets.notes: Largest Sun & Moon set at the time. Reintroduced the Lost Zone mechanic. Spawned multiple competitive archetypes including Lost March and Blacephalon-GX Beast Ring.

sets.name: Team Up
sets.notes: Introduced TAG TEAM Pokémon-GX — paired Pokémon on single cards with high HP and GX attacks. Pikachu & Zekrom-GX defined Lightning-type decks for years.

sets.name: Detective Pikachu
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. Tiny 18-card set tied to Detective Pikachu movie. Sold through special movie promotional blisters only. Niche collectible.

sets.name: Unbroken Bonds
sets.notes: Reshiram & Charizard-GX became iconic chase card. One of the largest Sun & Moon sets. Green's Exploration became a competitive staple Supporter.

sets.name: Unified Minds
sets.notes: Mewtwo & Mew-GX was a flexible TAG TEAM (copying attacks from Psychic Pokémon in discard). Set also featured first TAG TEAM Trainer-style illustrations.

sets.name: Hidden Fates
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. 68-card main set + 94-card Shiny Vault sub-set = 162 cards total (plus a secret rare). Shiny Charizard-GX (SV49/SV94) is one of the most iconic modern chase cards. Sealed products (especially tins) have appreciated significantly. Defining 'Fates' line set.

sets.name: Cosmic Eclipse
sets.notes: Largest Pokémon TCG set at release (272 cards). Era-closing capstone with three-Pokémon TAG TEAMs and TAG TEAM Supporter cards (paired Trainers on single card). Arceus & Dialga & Palkia-GX saw heavy competitive play.

eras.character: Gen VIII. Introduced Pokémon V and VMAX (Dynamax/Gigantamax), then VSTAR. The era that coincided with COVID pandemic hobby boom. Evolving Skies produced Moonbreon — arguably the most iconic modern chase card. Alternate Art treatments became a defining collector format. Radiant Pokémon introduced late-era.

sets.name: Sword & Shield
sets.notes: Base set of Sword & Shield era. Introduced V and VMAX mechanics. Galar region focus. Zacian V and Zamazenta V as legendary starters.

sets.name: Rebel Clash
sets.notes: Boss's Orders became a defining competitive Supporter of the SWSH era. Galarian starter VMAXes featured.

sets.name: Darkness Ablaze
sets.notes: Launched at peak pandemic TCG hype. Charizard VMAX (Rainbow Rare) became one of the chase cards of 2020. Sealed product from this era saw huge appreciation. Eternatus VMAX dominated competitive play.

sets.name: Champion's Path
sets.notes: Small 80-card set sold only through special collections (no standalone booster boxes). Charizard VMAX Rainbow Rare is the signature chase — historically one of the most expensive modern Charizard cards. Extreme sealed scarcity at launch.

sets.name: Vivid Voltage
sets.notes: Pikachu VMAX Rainbow Rare became a top chase card. Introduced Amazing Rare cards (unique etched foil style). Launched during peak pandemic hobby boom.

sets.name: Shining Fates
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. 73 main cards + 122-card Shiny Vault sub-set. Spiritual successor to Hidden Fates. Shiny Charizard VMAX was the centerpiece. Sold in special products (tins, Elite Trainer Boxes), no standard booster boxes.

sets.name: Battle Styles
sets.notes: Introduced Single Strike and Rapid Strike card subtypes. Urshifu VMAXes as signature cards. Mechanic would define the mid-SWSH competitive meta.

sets.name: Chilling Reign
sets.notes: Shadow Rider Calyrex VMAX and Ice Rider Calyrex VMAX dominated competitive play for months. First set with widespread alternate art full-body treatments. Crown Tundra DLC tie-in.

sets.name: Evolving Skies
sets.notes: The defining modern chase set. All 8 Eeveelutions got VMAX treatments with alternate art. Umbreon VMAX Alt Art ('Moonbreon') by illustrator Keiichiro Ito became arguably the most iconic modern Pokemon card. Sealed product from this set has had exceptional long-term appreciation. Historical benchmark for modern sealed investing. Approx 340+ card master set including reverse holos and secret rares.
sets.market_notes: Observed April 2026: despite being the most iconic Sword & Shield era set, Evolving Skies singles (top 20 by value) have underperformed peer SWSH sets in month-over-month growth over the trailing 12 months — only 3 green months vs 6-8 for most peer sets, and current streak of 1 positive month vs 3-4 for peers. Source: external analysis observed in Pika Pika Papa SWSH dashboard (Apr 2026 video). Implication: significant latent upside remains for chase singles despite sealed appreciation. Catch'em should verify pattern on own daily data once sufficient history accumulated.

sets.name: Celebrations
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. 25th Anniversary set. 25 main modern cards + 25-card Classic Collection featuring reprints of iconic vintage cards with anniversary stamp. V-Union debuted (4-piece assembly cards). Sold only in special collections. Highly collectible as anniversary milestone.

sets.name: Fusion Strike
sets.notes: Introduced Fusion Strike mechanic. One of the largest SWSH-era sets. Mew VMAX became a top competitive deck. Gengar VMAX Alt Art gained collector chase status.

sets.name: Brilliant Stars
sets.notes: Introduced Pokémon VSTAR mechanic (star powers, once-per-game). Debuted Trainer Gallery sub-set — cards with unique illustrator artwork, numbered TG01/TG30. Charizard VSTAR became a chase card.

sets.name: Astral Radiance
sets.notes: Tied to Pokémon Legends Arceus. Introduced Radiant Pokémon (mirror-foil single-copy deck cards). Origin Forme Palkia VSTAR saw heavy competitive play.

sets.name: Pokémon GO
sets.notes: Pokémon GO mobile game crossover set. Radiant Charizard gained chase status. Small special set sold via special products (not standard booster boxes). Ditto V transformation gimmick.

sets.name: Lost Origin
sets.notes: Lost Zone mechanic returned. Giratina VSTAR became a dominant Lost Zone archetype pillar that persisted for years. Large set (247 cards).

sets.name: Silver Tempest
sets.notes: Lugia VSTAR Alt Art is one of the signature Alt Art chase cards of the SWSH era. Alolan Vulpix VSTAR became a key competitive draw engine.

sets.name: Crown Zenith
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. Final Sword & Shield era set. 160 main cards + 70-card Galarian Gallery sub-set. Galarian Gallery featured special illustration cards with unique art — predecessor to Scarlet & Violet Illustration Rares. Era-closing capstone. Sold only in special products (ETBs, collections) — no standard booster boxes.

eras.character: Gen IX. Paldea region. Returned to yellow borders and classic card back design. Pokémon ex (lowercase) replaced V/VSTAR. Illustration Rare and Special Illustration Rare became defining collector formats. Prismatic Evolutions and 151 created hobby-wide chase frenzies. Black Bolt / White Flare split-release format debuted.

sets.name: Scarlet & Violet
sets.notes: Base set of Scarlet & Violet era. Reset the card design back to classic yellow borders. Introduced the new Pokémon ex mechanic and Illustration Rare rarity tier. Paldea region starters featured.

sets.name: Paldea Evolved
sets.notes: Massive 279-card set. Paldean starter final evolutions as ex cards. Gardevoir ex and Chien-Pao ex became defining competitive cards. First-year Scarlet & Violet cornerstone.

sets.name: Obsidian Flames
sets.notes: Tera Charizard ex (Dark-type, #125/197 with SIR at #215/197) became a major chase card. Showcased the type-shifting aspect of Terastallization. Charizard as a Darkness-type Tera was a major visual / thematic statement.

Nostalgia-driven special expansion covering only the original 151 Kanto Pokémon. Launched to massive demand and sustained scarcity. SIR Mew ex is the signature chase. Set sold out at retail for extended periods post-launch. Became a benchmark for how nostalgia + scarcity drives modern sealed demand.

sets.name: Paradox Rift
sets.notes: Introduced Ancient and Future sub-types (Paradox Pokémon from Area Zero). Mechanics impacted competitive deck building. Roaring Moon ex saw extended tournament relevance.

sets.name: Paldean Fates
key_mechanics: 130+ Shiny Pokémon reprints with new art
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. 91 main card numbers but 245 cards total due to Shiny subset. Continuation of the Hidden Fates / Shining Fates lineage. Bubble Mew (Shiny illustration rare) became a signature chase. Shiny variants of existing Scarlet & Violet cards with unique art treatments.

sets.name: Temporal Forces
sets.notes: Continuation of Paradox Pokémon theme from Paradox Rift. Raging Bolt ex and Gouging Fire ex became key competitive cards.

sets.name: Twilight Masquerade
sets.notes: Tied to Scarlet & Violet: The Teal Mask DLC. Four Ogerpon ex variants (Teal, Wellspring, Hearthflame, Cornerstone masks). Greninja ex was a major chase card.

sets.name: Shrouded Fable
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. Small 99-card special expansion tied to Indigo Disk DLC content. Curated format — sold through ETBs and collections, no standard booster boxes.

sets.name: Stellar Crown
key_mechanics: Stellar Tera Pokémon ex mechanic debut
sets.notes: Introduced Stellar Tera Pokémon ex — a new variant of Tera with rainbow typing. Terapagos ex as legendary cover card. Bridge to Prismatic Evolutions Stellar Tera Eeveelution theme.

sets.name: Surging Sparks
sets.notes: Pikachu ex (especially SIR) became a major chase card. Large 252-card set with strong Illustration Rare lineup. Served as direct lead-in to Prismatic Evolutions.

sets.name: Prismatic Evolutions
key_mechanics: Poké Ball / Master Ball parallel foils debut
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. Eeveelution-focused special expansion. Spiritual successor to Evolving Skies for the Paldea era. Introduced parallel foil patterns (Poké Ball foil on commons/uncommons, rarer Master Ball foil). Umbreon ex SIR ('Sunbreon') became the defining chase card of the set — echoing Moonbreon. Launched to extreme demand with retail shortages, restocks promised by TPCi. Among the most hyped modern sets ever.

sets.name: Journey Together
sets.notes: First main set of 2025. Introduced Trainer-owned named Pokémon (N's, Lillie's, etc.) — mechanic echoed in later Destined Rivals. Emphasis on character + Pokémon bonds.

sets.name: Destined Rivals
sets.notes: Continued Trainer-owned Pokémon theme. Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex as flagship. Featured a wide range of rival/Trainer-owned Pokémon mechanics. Strong collector appeal via character-driven illustrations.

sets.name: Black Bolt
sets.notes: First half of the split-release duo. Zekrom-themed counterpart to White Flare. Paired simultaneous release format was a first for English TCG. Heavy Unova region reference. Released alongside White Flare on the same date.

sets.name: White Flare
sets.notes: Second half of the split-release duo. Reshiram-themed counterpart to Black Bolt. The two sets were sold as separate products with distinct but overlapping themes. Released alongside Black Bolt. Final Scarlet & Violet era set.

eras.character: Gen IX continues with a mechanical reset. Mega Evolution Pokémon ex reintroduced as headline mechanic (tied to Pokémon Legends: Z-A game). Gold Hyper Rares debuted as new top rarity tier. First era to launch simultaneously worldwide for 30th anniversary. Active/ongoing era as of Apr 2026.

sets.name: Mega Evolution
sets.notes: Era-launching base set. English combines Japan's Mega Brave + Mega Symphonia sets. Introduced Gold Hyper Rare as a new rarity above Special Illustration Rare. Tied to Pokémon Legends: Z-A game (launched Oct 2025). First era since XY to feature Mega Evolution as mechanic. FLAG: Card count approximate (~175) — verify against official card list.

sets.name: Phantasmal Flames
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. English counterpart to Japan's Inferno X. Mega Charizard X ex as flagship card. Smaller ~94-card main set count. FLAG: Card count approximate — verify against final card list.

sets.name: Ascended Heroes
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. First 2026 set and largest English set of Mega Evolution era to date (~290 cards). English counterpart to Japan's Mega Dream. Split release: Tech Sticker Collection Jan 30 → ETB Feb 20 → Booster Bundles Apr 23. Mega Dragonite ex reported at ~1-in-70-90 pack pull rate by Beckett. FLAG: Pull rate data cited from Beckett reporting — verify if using in public content.
sets.release_schedule: Split release: Tech Sticker Collection 2026-01-30, ETB 2026-02-20, Booster Bundle 2026-04-24, Mega ex Boxes 2026-04-23

sets.name: Perfect Order
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. Third Mega Evolution main set. Smaller curated card count (~88 main + secret rares for 120+ total). Mega Zygarde ex as cover star. Tied to Pokémon Legends: Z-A and Lumiose City setting. Prereleases held Mar 14+.

sets.name: Chaos Rising
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. Fourth Mega Evolution main set (upcoming as of Apr 2026). English counterpart to Japan's Ninja Spinner. Mega Greninja ex is the flagship. Smaller set (~86 main, 120+ with secret rares). Card list still being revealed at this database build date. FLAG: Pre-release data — verify card count once officially listed.

sets.name: Pitch Black
sets.notes: NO standalone Booster Box for this special/mini-set expansion. Upcoming set as of Apr 2026. English counterpart to Japan's Abyss Eye. Mega Darkrai focus. Card count not yet confirmed. FLAG: Pre-release — verify all data when announced.

sets.name: 30th Anniversary Celebration
